svg.text: FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure (FTI) Ground Stop Architecture
Network flooding, potential source disconnection, and fail-safe airspace ground stop (Nov 13, 2026)

g.text: 1. Network Flooding
Hypothesis
FTI Modernization & Potential Sources
FAA modernizing telecommunications infrastructure.
High-rate connection flood (~1,000 req / 4-5s) hit backbone.
El Dorado and Amarillo identified as potential sources.
Contractor L3Harris disconnected both sites to halt flood.
Root cause remains under active formal FAA investigation.
Hypothetical Reconnect Flood
Model: Systems analysis of high-rate connection storm.
Unthrottled discovery or reconnect retries flood backbone.
High packet volume fills switch buffers to capacity.
Buffer saturation causes tail drops of real-time packets.
17 regional air traffic centers lose radar feeds.
Hypothetical Route Instability Model
Model: Protocol misconfiguration evaluates route flapping.
Rapid routing updates consume switch management CPU.
Linecard queues drop time-critical radar packets.
Network latency surges, dropping inter-center heartbeats.
Demonstrates buffer starvation dynamics in private IP meshes.
2. Buffer Exhaustion
Cascade
Linecard Buffer Tail-Drop
Intermediary FTI backbone switches filled buffers.
FIFO queues dropped arriving real-time packets.
Radar plots and ADS-B feeds suffered 60%+ loss.
Inter-facility voice loops experienced static jitter.
17 of 22 regional ARTCC centers lost radar feeds.
ERAM Fail-Safe Watchdogs
En Route Automation Modernization requires sub-50ms
telemetry heartbeats to guarantee separation.
When telemetry dropped, safety watchdogs tripped.
Air traffic controllers lost automated track radar.
Safety protocol mandated departure suspension.
15:50 ET Ground Stop Order
FAA command center ordered national ground stop.
All commercial domestic flights held at gates.
Airborne planes (~3,500) maintained TCAS & landed.
Ground halt lasted approximately 4.5 hours.
Over 5,000 nationwide flights delayed or canceled.
3. Node Disconnection
Resolution
Potential Source Disconnection
L3Harris isolated El Dorado and Amarillo nodes.
Sites disconnected to halt flooding traffic.
Backbone latency stabilized upon disconnection.
Packet drop rate collapsed across regional paths.
Telemetry links restored normal responsiveness.
Radar Stream Re-synchronization
ERAM platforms verified track plot consistency.
TRACON and tower audio channels tested clear.
Telemetry packet drops returned to zero.
Redundant TDM circuits confirmed intact as backup.
All 17 ARTCC facilities cleared for departures.
20:15 ET Resumption of Air Traffic
FAA officially lifted nationwide ground stop.
Airports staggered departures to manage runway queues.
FAA investigated potential source configurations.
Incident triggered congressional modernizing reviews.
Residual flight delays normalized over next 48 hours.
4. Engineering Safeguards & Telecom Modernization Mitigations
Control Plane Rate Limiting & VRF Isolation
1. Control Plane Policing (CoPP): Enforce strict rate limits on broadcast,
BGP, and OSPF discovery frames to prevent CPU starvation.
2. VRF Segmentation: Isolate newly migrated IP edge segments from the core
air traffic telemetry mesh until routing tables reach verified convergence.
3. Automated Port Dampening: Automatically shut down flapping interfaces
exceeding threshold reconnection attempts within a rolling 10-second window.
4. Fail-Safe Airspace Procedures: Redundant independent sensors ensure that
airborne flights land safely even if ground departure automation halts.
Zero airborne safety incidents occurred during the 4.5-hour ground stop.
Canary Verification Checklist for Critical Networks
1. Canary Interface Verification: New routers must run in passive listen mode
for a minimum of 24 hours prior to carrying active radar or audio data.
2. Linecard Buffer Telemetry: Alert on buffer queue utilization exceeding 40%
to identify head-of-line blocking before real-time tail drops manifest.
3. Automated Circuit Rollback: If inter-facility telemetry drops exceed 0.01%,
failover orchestrator automatically falls back to verified parallel circuits.
4. Staggered Migration Windows: Pausing deployments across regional ARTCCs
confines faults to single sectors without impacting national airspace.
Guarantees high-assurance continuity for critical civilian infrastructure.
